- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ -0.33) and prices are trending down, model often undercorrects; increase forecast slightly to reflect mean reversion.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., 70+ to 72+), especially if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish — cap forecast at +2–3% above recent peak to avoid lagged overcorrection.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust quickly; apply a 1–2 day lag correction downward.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates mean reversion in volatile periods — add 0.5–1.0% buffer to forecast if sentiment is mixed or trending sideways.
- If sentiment is consistently positive but price is declining, model may misread sentiment — adjust forecast to reflect sentiment-weighted mean rather than pure trend.
